items.title: An auto-homotopy exists as soon as one self-path is central and every point is merely connected to the basepoint

items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:autohtpy` at source lines 77-85: if a = a is a set, every x : A is merely equal to a, and q commutes with every self-path of a, then there is f : prd x:A (x = x) with f(a) = q. The author's proof (source lines 86-118) is one of the more delicate arguments of the chapter because the obvious definition cannot be written: g(x) inhabits a truncation and the target type x = x is not a proposition, so the proof first establishes that all path types of A are sets (lines 87-92), then replaces the naive formula by the uniquely characterised type B(x) (lines 94-101) and proves that B(x) is a mere proposition by a coherence argument that consumes transport in identity and function types (lines 102-110), and only then inhabits B(x) with the candidate opp p `ct` q `ct` p, whose verification reduces to the centrality hypothesis (lines 112-117). The statement exhibits none of the three stages and hides why the naive definition fails.
